authoritative_claim.section: 52. A finite approximation with an explicit price
authoritative_claim.proposition: P47. Polyhedral approximation of the rotation model

claim_card.objects: State = Fin 3 -> Real, mass z=z 0, initial=(1,1,0). Actual rotate matrix diag(1,alpha R), with R=[[3/5,-4/5],[4/5,3/5]]. Probe/reset branches are retained. Actual regular n-gon vertices are exp(2*pi*i*j/n), embedded at mass one as columns of vertexSynthesis n. The policy is a shared action-probability kernel on each joint action/observation history.
claim_card.coefficient_domains: General operators, synthesis and positive lifts over Real; explicit alpha=2/3 certificate data are exhibited over Rational and cast into Real.
claim_card.hypotheses: For the regular polygon n>=3, alpha>=0 and alpha<=cos(pi/n). For the common-Lorentz law bound 0<=alpha<=1 and every history policy is a probability vector, including zero action weights. Diamond: 0<=alpha<=5/7. Vertex budget: 0<eta<=1 and alpha=1-eta.
conclusions: Actual regular-vertex synthesis is surjective; its positive generated cone is invariant under every modified branch and contains the declared initial state.
Exist nonnegative lifted branch matrices, a normalized nonnegative initial vector, exact synthesis/intertwining and per-action column mass one, with equality of every finite word probability.

Exact and attenuated models are valid on the same constructed Lorentz probability cone. Actual observation-law TV under every common randomized history policy at every natural horizon T is <=min(1,T*(1-alpha)/2).
The actual Lorentz base norm, defined from positive-decomposition cost infima, equals max(abs(t),sqrt(x^2+y^2)); the discrepancy estimate is derived from this norm.
The explicit four-generator diamond is exactly abs(x)+abs(y)<=t and gives a positive lift for alpha<=5/7. At alpha=2/3 all synthesis, branch and initial-prior data are literal casts of rational data.
For eta in (0,1], n=max(3,ceilNat(pi/sqrt(2*eta))) supplies the actual regular-vertex finite certificate with attenuation alpha=1-eta.

sufficient_vertex_positive_lift uses n=max(3,ceilNat(pi/sqrt(2*eta))) and the proved RegularPolygon.sufficient_vertex_count, then derives alpha=1-eta>=0 from eta<=1. The cosine condition supplies all actual regular-lift obligations.

n>=3 prevents zero denominators and gives positive inradius for surjectivity. alpha=0, eta=1 and T=0 are admitted. Policy weights may vanish; no likelihood margin or reciprocal action probability is used. The common-cone comparison also permits alpha=1 and then yields zero discrepancy; the finite regular-polygon condition itself excludes alpha=1 for finite n>=3.
